minutes.headline: Select Board found two dogs dangerous after a goat was killed; ordered pen, muzzles, insurance, restitution
minutes.summary: A public dog hearing over an August attack that killed a neighbors' goat took most of the meeting; the owner did not appear and the board unanimously found the dogs dangerous and imposed conditions. The board also ranked and committed ARPA funds in one combined motion, ratified two appointments, authorized a letter to DOR, reviewed special town meeting articles, accepted the town manager's goals and approved minutes.

what_happened.line: The Select Board unanimously deemed two dogs dangerous after an August attack that killed a neighbors' goat; the owner did not appear.
The board unanimously ordered a pen, muzzles, insurance, identification and restitution, with 60 days to comply and a new hearing on any violation.
The board committed ARPA funds to the ranked requests in one combined motion, with pilot funds specified for the Keating well; the Flat Hill drainage request was held a week.
The board authorized the chair to sign the letter to DOR for third quarter preliminary tax bills.
The board accepted the town manager's fiscal year 2024 goals and ratified two appointments; articles for the special town meeting are due the 18th.

why_it_matters: The ARPA vote spends the last of the town's federal relief money on water, library, school, municipal building and sewer manhole projects, and the sewer request is tied to a stabilization vote for vehicles that residents may be asked to take at the fall town meeting.
The third quarter preliminary tax bill letter to DOR sets the timing of when the next installment of a property tax bill is issued.
The dangerous-dog order sets restitution and insurance conditions on the owner and gives the board a basis to hold a new hearing if the conditions are broken.
watch_next: Next week's meeting: the held Flat Hill drainage ARPA request.
The 18th: deadline for articles for the special town meeting, including the opioid settlement fund article the board will discuss with the police chief.

Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the main votes and most dollar figures. Most differences are caption mishearings of names and digits. The substantive ones are the dog-restrictions order (ours says passed unanimously, the official minutes give no outcome), the opioid article amount ($80,000 officially, not the figures we heard), and the chair's insurance proposal ($1,000,000,000 officially, one million in ours). Check those three against the recording first.
